newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: IMF extends Venezuela stand-by program 18 months.
newsitem.headline: IMF extends Venezuela stand-by program 18 months.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund approved Wednesday a Venezuelan request to extend its stand-by program with the country for another 18 months, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
The Venezuelan Finance Ministry said Matos had announced news of the program extension in an interview with local journalists by telephone from Washington.
"The IMF is prepared to support the country," Matos said after a meeting with IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus, a Finance Ministry statement said.
Venezuela's current 12-month stand-by program with the IMF is due to expire in July.
Matos said the IMF would support Venezuela's reforms, but would not be loaning it any more money.
Windfall oil revenues last year saw Venezuela cancel a $1.4 billion stand-by loan shortly after receiving the first $500 million tranche.
"The most important thing is that although Venezuela still has additional oil revenues, it has shown that it is prepared to continue along the path of fiscal discipline," he added.

Venezuela, widely lauded for strides made during the first year of an economic reform program, has been warned by analysts and IMF officials not to loosen its tight grip on fiscal accounts due to the unexpected windfall it received last year from high oil prices.
